examples.knowledge_point: Factoring a Sum of Higher-Degree Squares
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since

$$
25x^4 + 4 y^8 = \left( 5x^2\right)^2 + \left(2 y^4\right)^2.
$$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using $\textrm{i}^2 = -1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}25{x}^{4}+4{y}^{8} & =25{x}^{4}-(-4{y}^{8}) \\  & =25{x}^{4}-(4{\text{i}}^{2}{y}^{8}) \\  & ={(5{x}^{2})}^{2}-{(2\text{i}{y}^{4})}^{2} \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+2\text{i}{y}^{4})(5{x}^{2}-2\text{i}{y}^{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}9{w}^{2}+16 & =9{w}^{2}-(-16) \\  & =9{w}^{2}-(16{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =(3w)^{2}-{(4\text{i})}^{2} \\  & =(3w+4\text{i})(3w-4\text{i}).\end{aligned}
$$
